key_insight: Automatically generated derivatives enable differentiable high-order mesh r-adaptivity with accurate optimization gradients, Hessians, and mesh sensitivities.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports adaptive finite element meshing and consistent sensitivity analysis for inverse engineering problems while reducing manual derivative development.
method: Define local mesh-quality objectives using the Target-Matrix Optimization Paradigm.
Use ∂FEM to generate pointwise first, second, and mixed derivatives, then assemble finite element operators.
Apply Hessians matrix-free on CPUs and GPUs and obtain mesh sensitivities by implicit differentiation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments report GPU solve times comparable to hand-derived TMOP implementations on a benchmark, improved r-adaptivity convergence, and material-interface identification in inverse heat conduction.
watch_item: Consistent mesh sensitivities rely on sufficiently converged stationarity equations and a well-conditioned Hessian solve.
